sources.title: Go Language Specification - channel types
claims: capacity zero means an unbuffered channel; communication succeeds only when sender and receiver are ready

sources.title: Go Memory Model - channel communication
claims: channel send/receive operations provide synchronization edges defined by the Go memory model

sources.title: Go runtime chan.go
claims: channel implementation uses a lock and send/receive wait queues
blocking channel paths represent waiting goroutines with sudog records and use runtime park/ready machinery

sources.title: Go runtime HACKING - scheduler structures
claims: G is a goroutine, M is an OS thread, P carries resources required to execute Go code
the scheduler matches G, M and P rather than equating a goroutine with an OS thread

sources.title: sync.WaitGroup package documentation
claims: WaitGroup waits for a collection of tasks; Add establishes the count and Done decrements it
